A 57 second note for Medeloop

Recorded for the Chief Commercial Officer search. Press play.
Hi, I'm Manish Agarwal. Medeloop is hiring a Chief Commercial Officer for reasons I can point to directly in the posting. First, Early traction is founder-driven; without a codified, repeatable motion, revenue cannot scale past the first anchor accounts. As CRO in private equity I have taken four portfolio companies from early traction to a repeatable motion, seven point four million in ARR across more than sixty-five enterprise clients. Second, Selling AI into providers, payers, and government demands regulated-industry credibility most commercial leaders simply do not have. I ran healthcare integration at Vorro, FHIR and healthcare data pipes moving ten million transactions a day, and I scaled that business threefold at forty-seven percent EBITDA selling into regulated enterprises. Third, No commercial operating discipline exists yet; the board cannot trust forecasts, and leadership is flying without instruments. At Sterling I installed the forecasting and governance discipline that carried us through IPO preparation, holding ninety percent enterprise retention while valuation grew ten percent. If that maps to what Medeloop is working on, I would enjoy comparing notes on how I would approach the first ninety days… Thanks for listening.
